Trevor —

Thanks for sending these over and for the quick summary. We're almost there; finance needs a couple of standard items before we can activate payee routing to an escrow account: 

Required for vendor activation:
- Completed W-9 (legal entity must match account owner on bank letter)
- Voided check or bank letter on bank letterhead with bank contact and signature (you’ve provided the bank letter which is great)
- Signed escrow agreement showing Harbor Escrow Services as the payee administrator

For our PO/invoice routing, we need a structured remit string so our PayOps can auto-attach invoices to POs. Sample format we prefer: "PO=REDW-<PO#>;INV=<Invoice#>;VEND=Harbor Logistics" — please confirm if Harbor can emit that on the invoice PDF or in the remittance field when sending electronic invoices.

Marissa and Marcus — please advise if we need additional fintech confirmation for escrow-owned accounts (Marissa: any compliance flags here?).

If everything checks out with the W-9 and signed escrow agreement, we'll run a one-time bank verification (micro-deposits) or accept the bank letter plus escrow agreement per our payee activation checklist.

Thanks — attaching the Redwood payee-activation checklist in case it helps (internal reference).

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Trevor / Sofia —

Appreciate the prompt follow-up and the attachments — W-9 and bank letter are in our portal. I reviewed the escrow agreement and cleared it with our compliance checklist. We can accept a vendor-managed escrow for the initial onboarding remittance under the following conditions: 

1) Invoice remit must include the structured string exactly as specified so our AP system can auto-match. Final accepted format: "PO=REDW-<PO#>;INV=<Invoice#>;VEND=Harbor Logistics" (case-insensitive).
2) For the first payment, PayOps will run a micro-deposit verification to the escrow account. If the micro-deposits reconcile, we’ll mark the payee active and schedule the first remittance for the next AP cycle (estimated: 2028-07-27).
3) If Harbor prefers to skip micro-deposits, we will accept the bank letter + escrow agreement only if Harbor Escrow Services provides a bank-signed verification email from bank-escrow@harborexamplebank.com confirming the account name and masking policy.

Action items: 
- Trevor: confirm whether you want RedWood to run micro-deposits to the escrow account (we will need the exact last-4 to reconcile), or arrange for the bank-signed verification email.
- Harbor Accounting: please reply with final decision and confirm the invoice remit format so we can lock the PO mapping rule.

Once we receive that, I’ll update the payee record and share the activation note. Attached is our internal payee-activation-checklist.pdf for your reference.

Best,
